consulates.note: All Ottawa addresses below were verified from Global Affairs Canada's 'Foreign Representatives in Canada' directory on 2026-10-27 (page last modified 2025-01-22). That directory page lists addresses only, not phone numbers or hours — check the directory before visiting or calling, as details can change. Two Ottawa listings (Burundi and Luxembourg) show no street address in the directory, listed here as 'To be determined'. Missions whose listed address is outside Ottawa (for example in Washington, D.C., New York, or Singapore) are not included in this Ottawa list; see the full directory for those.

fatwa_citations_used: Work in pork/alcohol restaurants, including dishwashing, as cooperation in sin (Qur'an 5:2) — Permanent Committee / Ibn Baz, Fatawa al-Lajnah al-Daa'imah 14/414, as recorded in the previous coordinator report. Site screening follows the user's stricter spec: any role in such a restaurant is rejected.

Ramadan obligation and sick/traveller make-up — Ibn Baz, Ibn Uthaymeen, as recorded in the previous coordinator report. Pregnancy detail is covered in 'scholar_difference' (scholars differ; no ruling given).
Zakat 2.5%, silver nisab 595 g (Ibn Baz favoured), eight recipients Qur'an 9:60 — as recorded in the previous coordinator report.
Funeral washing and four-takbeer prayer — Ibn Baz, Majmu' 13/123, as recorded in the previous coordinator report. Shrouding detail is covered in 'scholar_difference' (no finished ruling given).
Congregational prayer obligation — Ibn Baz, Ibn Uthaymeen, as recorded in the previous coordinator report.
Halal meat: naming Allah essential — Ibn Uthaymeen, Ibn Baz, Al-Albani, as recorded in the previous coordinator report.
Alcohol/pork/gambling advertising and work prohibited — Ibn Baz, Ibn Uthaymeen, as recorded in the previous coordinator report.

guides.food: Practical guide: look for a halal certification mark you recognise, ask the restaurant or shop what certification it uses, and check ingredients for pork, gelatin, and alcohol. The site never lists a restaurant or business that sells alcohol or pork, gambling, or any doubtful business. For questions where scholars differ, see 'Questions where scholars differ' on this site. This site gives no ruling of its own.
guides.funeral: Practical guide: in Canada, contact the funeral home, the hospital or coroner, and your local mosque or community organisation as soon as possible; ask about washing, shrouding, prayer, burial, and the death certificate and registration steps in your province. For questions where scholars differ, including shrouding detail, see the section 'Questions where scholars differ' on this site.
guides.mosques: Practical guide: search for a mosque or prayer space in your city, check its prayer times and Friday prayer time on its own website or notice board, and ask about newcomer welcome, English classes, and community help. This site gives no ruling of its own.
guides.pregnancy: Practical guide: register for your province's health coverage as soon as you arrive, find a family doctor, midwife, or obstetrician through your province's health line, and ask about prenatal classes, baby supplies, and community support in your city. This guide gives practical steps only; it does not give medical advice or a religious ruling.
guides.ramadan: Practical guide: Ramadan dates change each year — check a local mosque or Islamic calendar for the current year's dates, Suhoor/Iftar times, and Taraweeh times. For questions where scholars differ, see the section 'Questions where scholars differ' on this site.
guides.zakat: Practical guide: Zakat is 2.5% on qualifying wealth held for a lunar year, with a silver nisab of 595 grams, and eight recipient categories in Qur'an 9:60. Use a calculator only as an estimate, and ask a knowledgeable scholar or local mosque for a personal calculation — the site does not give a personal fatwa.

note: Practical newcomer guides only. Religious rulings are NOT given as the site's own opinion. Where a ruling is cited, it is from the scholars named in the citation. Topics with no clear ruling agreed by Ibn Baz, Ibn Uthaymeen, and Al-Albani, or with a conflict among them, are in 'scholar_difference' and are NOT written as finished rulings.

scholar_difference.title: Questions where scholars differ
scholar_difference.intro: This site does not give a ruling of its own on the questions below. In the research for this site, no single clear ruling was found that is agreed by Ibn Baz, Ibn Uthaymeen, and Al-Albani together. Where scholars differ, this site describes the difference in plain words and does not choose between the positions. For your own situation, ask a trusted scholar.

topics.title: Fasting in Ramadan during pregnancy
topics.body: Scholars differ on what a pregnant woman who does not fast in Ramadan should do afterwards: whether she makes up the missed days, or feeds a poor person for each missed day instead, or both. A Permanent Committee fatwa chaired by Ibn Baz (Fatwa No. 1144) says a pregnant woman who fears harm for herself or her child may break the fast and make up the missed days, like a sick person. A feeding-only position is also reported in summaries attributed to Al-Albani, but this site could not verify that position from a primary fatwa source in this round, so it is not presented here as a verified attribution. Because the positions differ, this site gives no ruling here. Ask a trusted scholar for your own situation, and also ask your doctor about fasting and your health.

topics.title: Shrouding detail at a funeral
topics.body: This site gives practical steps for contacting a funeral home, hospital or coroner, and mosque, and for asking about washing, prayer, burial, and registration. It does not give a finished ruling on shrouding detail, because no directly attributed fatwa from Ibn Baz, Ibn Uthaymeen, and Al-Albani together was found in this research that settles that detail. Ask a trusted scholar or your local mosque for guidance for a particular case.

topics.title: General cleaning work in a place that serves forbidden food or drink
topics.body: This site's own screening is strict and stays strict: it never lists a job with a restaurant or business that serves pork or alcohol, in any role, including kitchen help and dishwashing. That screening is the site's own rule for what it lists, not a ruling on every kind of cleaning work. A distinction between dishwashing and general cleaning of a place, chairs, or windows was raised in one source in earlier research, but no clear single ruling from Ibn Baz, Ibn Uthaymeen, and Al-Albani together was found that settles indirect cleaning cases. Ask a trusted scholar about a particular job.

topics.title: Mixed businesses and separate departments
topics.body: This site does not give a ruling on working for a mixed business, or in a separate department of a business that also sells forbidden goods. No clear single ruling from Ibn Baz, Ibn Uthaymeen, and Al-Albani together was found in this research that settles these cases. The site's own listing rule stays strict: it does not list alcohol, pork, gambling, or doubtful businesses. For a particular job, ask a trusted scholar.

scholar_difference.sources_consulted: Permanent Committee for Scholarly Research and Ifta, Fatwa No. 1144 (pregnancy and breastfeeding, make-up position); Ibn Baz, 30 Questions and Answers on Fasting (pregnancy make-up wording); secondary summaries reporting a feeding-only position attributed to Al-Albani, not verified from a primary source in this round and therefore not attributed as verified here.
